output.name: Ulsena
output.myth: Ulsena was a kelp-woman who lived in the cold shallows under the cliffs. One hot, calm day, which the old ones say never comes here, she climbed onto the rocks and married Ristan, a fisherman of the north skerry. He went out the next spring and the gale Tavo came laughing across the water and took his boat. Ulsena waited in the shallows. When no boat came back she did what kelp does when it wants the light. She grew. Her stalk went up past the seals, past the gulls, and when it left the water it kept going, because Aun had cut the string and nothing held the sky down any more. Her bulb is the crown at the top. Her long brown fronds still sway in the Unflown. Mother Hesk counts her turns and says she has not yet found him. Sailors say that on a calm night, if you hear a slow creak over the water, it is Ulsena, still looking.
output.verse:
Her stalk climbs past gulls,
through the cut string's empty air,
she sways, still searching.

The blue outline is a real silhouette offset from the gold lines, so it is not just a copy of the gold skeleton. However, the outline is thin and close to the gold lines, so the body mass is weak.

The crown float circle is a small hollow ring, so it does not read as a bride's veil or crown and works poorly as a head.
